set.body:
Current assessment and repair boundary

Sequential assessment 2026-09-12: retain P1 confirmed current defect. MultipleTesting.scala still counts null >= observed in plus-one pValues and returns Inclusive at the kth descending null in cutoff. ThresholdCutoff has only Inclusive/NoRejections; ThresholdCoreSuite still pins the inclusive numeric boundary. Direct source evaluation for nulls 1..19 and alpha .05 gives k=1, cutoff Inclusive(19), p(19)=2/20=.10. No new compiled probe was run here. Make the immediate repair independently reviewable within this mote: comparison semantics plus a supported decision method, exact agreement with the public p<=alpha rule including ties, finite extrema, attainable alpha and floating-point boundary behavior, and explicit legacy-double conversion policy. Then separately report broader statistical admission; repairing this deterministic boundary is not maxT/stepdown/HierScan certification. Current ThresholdMethod enum includes TFCE/cluster/RFT names without corresponding implementations in this module; do not advertise them as available. Preserve native null-family/identity, one/two-sided orientation and streaming requirements. Keep this mote open until its broader declared acceptance is qualified or explicitly split into separately tracked remaining scope.

Original report and broader qualification scope

Native threshold audit/admission requested by the PLS Neuro user for univariate voxelwise p-values and thresholding. Owner: ScalaFIM threshold with group/fit supplying valid statistic/null contracts; application integration is plsneuro bd-01M20V5F314V68XNY9SHDY4RR0 (foreign provenance, not a dependency edge).

Reproduced correctness defect: MaxNull.cutoff(Array(1.0,...,19.0), Alpha.unsafe(.05)) returns Inclusive(19.0), but MaxNull.pValueDoubles(Array(19.0), nulls) returns .10. An inclusive comparison rejects where adjustedP <= alpha does not. At nextUp(19.0), p=.05, so rejection requires a strict boundary. The existing ThresholdCoreSuite asserts the analogous inclusive boundary rather than checking agreement with the p-value. Probe compiled unchanged MultipleTesting.scala, Settings.scala, ThresholdError.scala plus the exact ThresholdCutoff ADT extracted from ThresholdResult.scala into isolated output; no native source changes. Reproducer /private/tmp/probe-threshold-cutoff.py; inputs/logs/hashes /private/tmp/scalafim-threshold-audit-20260909. Durable report/evidence will be /Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro/docs/verification/univariate-uncertainty-threshold-review-2026-09-09.md and .json.gz.

Required repair: typed cutoff comparison semantics agreeing with adjusted p decisions for ties, attainable alpha boundaries, smallest draw counts and finite extremes. Keep legacy numeric-threshold implications explicit. Regressions through public API on JVM and JS; exhaustive tiny distributions and an independent rank/count oracle.

Broader admission: inventory implemented vs enum-only/planned methods (current code has maxT, WY stepdown, HierScan; TFCE/cluster/RFT are not implemented by merely appearing in ThresholdMethod). Verify one/two-sided orientation on observed AND null fields; MC plus-one vs exact enumeration conventions/identity; common subject-bound null action across all voxels and blocks; declared fixed search mask, missing/failed samples and family across contrasts; subset-pivotal/other conditions for strong stepdown control; data-derived regions/priors and full adaptive HierScan search under the null. Calibrate spatial FWER/FDR on prespecified complete and partial-null fields with spatial dependence, small n, heterogeneity and supported first-level error estimation. p-to-mask/legend agreement and source-bound native/app round-trip evidence required. Streaming max-null reduction and deterministic scheduling should avoid a draws-by-voxels allocation for ordinary maxT.

Do not enable automatic significance thresholds from green unit tests alone; no statistical correction repairs invalid first-level SEs or invalid group/null modeling. This initial audit is a reproduced defect and qualification plan, not full-module certification.
